title: Va'etchanan: at home and on the way (Deuteronomy 6:7)
hookLine: talk of them sitting at home, walking by the way, lying down and rising up
carry: at home and on the way
tomorrow: Va'etchanan: the right and the good (Deuteronomy 6:18)

lines: IN THE CAR, EYES ON THE ROAD.
cards: The real conversations in a family often happen sideways. Not always at the formal dinner. Sometimes in the car, eyes on the road, when nobody has to look at anybody.
Or at the edge of a bed, lights off, when a kid suddenly asks the big question. Or in the kitchen at seven in the morning, half awake. The paragraph after the Shema seems to know this.
It doesn't schedule a weekly lesson. It names four ordinary places where words can be spoken, and an ordinary day already passes through them.

teach.b: The verse, in the old Jewish translation: "and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up."
Teach them diligently is one Hebrew word, v'shinantam, and early readers hear sharpen in it, while others hear repeat. Say it until it's sharp.
And talk of them, v'dibarta bam: not preach, talk. Then the four places. Sitting at home, walking on the road, lying down, rising up.
The rabbis read the last pair as times. That's why the Shema is said at night and in the morning. But they argued about the posture.

teach.h: LYING DOWN AND RISING: NIGHT AND MORNING.
teach.b: The school of Shammai said: at night, recline, and in the morning, stand, because the verse says lying down and rising up.

teach.h: HILLEL: AS YOU ARE, ON THE WAY.
teach.b: The school of Hillel said: everyone says it in their own way, however they happen to be, because the verse also says when thou walkest by the way.
Read that way, the verse isn't asking you to arrange your body for the words.

teach.h: AT HOME AND ON THE WAY.
teach.b: It's asking the words to come along wherever your body already is. The Mishnah even tells of Rabbi Tarfon, who lay down by the road at night to follow Shammai's ruling and put himself in danger from robbers.
His colleagues told him he deserved what nearly happened, for setting aside Hillel's view.

how: Jews say the Shema at night and in the morning, following the verse's lying down and rising up, and Jewish law follows the school of Hillel that it may be said in whatever position one happens to be.

o: and I listened: the portion of Sinai
and I taught: Moses' lessons for children
and I pleaded: the portion of the Shema

games.q: inside the four places — tap the pairs.
p: recline at night, stand at dawn

s: the verse sets a weekly time for teaching
it names four ordinary places: home, the road, lying down, rising up.
the rabbis read lying down and rising up as the times for the Shema
Jewish law follows Shammai: you must stand for the morning Shema
it follows Hillel: everyone says it as they happen to be.

games.q: it's night, you're traveling, and you want to say the Shema. Shammai says lie down. Hillel says as you are. what does the Mishnah's story warn?
o: Rabbi Tarfon lay down by the road and nearly met robbers.
Rabbi Tarfon stood and was scolded.
the rabbis said skip it when traveling.
games.why: he followed Shammai, lay down on the road and was in danger. his colleagues said he should have followed Hillel.

practice: Think of the four places in your own day: home, the road, bedtime, the morning. Pick the one that has another person in it, and one thing that matters to you that you haven't said in a while: a hope, a worry, a story.
Let it become a sentence or two you could say right where you already are.

wordCard.voice: Va'etchanan. And I pleaded. The portion that holds the Shema, and the four places its words are meant to travel.

orig.note: Hebrew: and thou shalt teach them diligently. some readers hear sharpen in it, others repeat.

carryVoice: Your line: at home and on the way. The week held eicha, the scouts, the gentle march, a pleading, a memory, the Shema, and now its places. Day four hundred ninety, in the books.
